title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Recent $6.56 weeks averaged 53 units (x1.18 vs baseline); one week sold 24 (x0.53), but that was outlier. No prior 2.3% increase. Price sensitivity moderate; expect slight decline.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. No past instances of delivery warnings. Demand may fall due to stockouts or reduced replenishment. Effect size uncertain.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 44.9. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 2.3% to $6.56, above regular $6.41. Recent weeks at $6.56 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) sold 24 and 53 units (vs baseline 44.9), averaging x1.18. This suggests modest price sensitivity but not a strong decline. Supplier delivery warning implies supply risk, lowering demand. No past price increase of this magnitude; only one past $6.56 week (x0.53), but that was in a low-demand week. Use noise-adjusted estimate from past price changes: no reliable lift or drop. Price increase likely suppresses demand. Confidence is low due to thin evidence and supply risk.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.9 | 5%-95%: 20.2 - 68.2 | 10%-90%: 26.8 - 64.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
